title: Claude Code: Agent Teams & Effort Controls
content:
## Overview

Alongside the Claude 5 model releases (see Claude Model History), Claude Code and the Claude API gained a cluster of related agentic features through mid-2026: **Agent Teams**, **effort controls**, **adaptive thinking**, and **context compaction**. Together they change how a Claude Code session decides how much reasoning to spend, how many agents to run at once, and how to keep working once a task outgrows the context window.

---

## Agent Teams (Research Preview)

Agent Teams lets Claude Code assemble **multiple agents that work in parallel and coordinate autonomously**, rather than a single coordinator dispatching one subagent at a time. It's best suited to tasks that split cleanly into independent, read-heavy work — for example, a codebase-wide review where each agent owns a different module or dimension (security, performance, style) and results are merged afterward.

This builds on the older single-coordinator subagent pattern (see Tool Use & Agents): instead of one Claude instance sequentially delegating and re-integrating, an agent team runs several delegate agents concurrently with their own coordination, closer to the parallel-fan-out patterns used by workflow orchestration.

---

## Effort Controls

Effort controls give developers an explicit dial on how much intelligence, speed, and cost a request uses. There are **four effort levels**:

- **low**
- **medium**
- **high** (default)
- **max**

At the default `high` level, the model uses extended thinking when it judges thinking will help; lowering or raising the level makes that judgment more or less selective. This replaces the older, manual `thinking: {type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}` API, which is now **removed** (returns a 400 error) on Sonnet 5, Opus 5, and Fable 5 — effort + adaptive thinking is the only supported path going forward.

```python
# Old (Sonnet 4.6 and earlier) — no longer supported on Sonnet 5 / Opus 5 / Fable 5
thinking = {"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": 32000}

# Current
thinking = {"type": "adaptive"}
# plus an effort level, e.g. "high" or "max", set via the effort parameter
```

---

## Adaptive Thinking

Adaptive thinking lets the model pick up on **contextual clues** in the request to decide, on its own, when deeper reasoning is worth the extra latency and tokens — rather than requiring the caller to pre-set a fixed thinking token budget. On Claude Sonnet 5 specifically, adaptive thinking is **on by default**: a request with no explicit `thinking` field now runs with adaptive thinking, a behavior change from Sonnet 4.6 (where no `thinking` field meant no thinking at all). Because `max_tokens` is a hard cap on thinking *plus* response text combined, workloads migrating from Sonnet 4.6 may need to raise `max_tokens` to avoid truncation.

---

## Context Compaction (Beta)

For long-running agentic tasks, context compaction automatically **summarizes and replaces older context** once a conversation approaches a configurable threshold — letting an agent keep working on a long task (e.g., a large refactor or multi-hour investigation) without hitting the context window ceiling. This is the API-level counterpart to Claude Code's `/compact` command and the automatic mid-session summarization Claude Code has long used to survive long sessions, now exposed as a configurable primitive for anyone building on the API directly.

---

## How These Fit Together

| Feature | Solves |
|---|---|
| Effort controls | Predictable cost/latency vs. capability trade-off, per request |
| Adaptive thinking | Removes the guesswork of manually sizing a thinking token budget |
| Context compaction | Lets a single agent run far longer without losing earlier context |
| Agent Teams | Lets *multiple* agents run the long task in parallel instead of one agent doing it serially |

For Claude Code users specifically, the practical effect is a session that can be tuned (via effort) for a quick fix vs. a deep investigation, that manages its own context automatically on long tasks, and that can — for read-heavy, parallelizable work — spin up a team instead of working through files one at a time.

---

## Other July 2026 Claude Code Updates

The same release cycle also shipped a VS Code Focus view, stronger sandbox credential masking, and improved plugin/MCP handling (including the MCP 2026-07-28 stateless spec — see that page for details), plus bug fixes to auto mode and cross-shell behavior.
